frames: each finger's body frames of the cad_v3 MJCF (assets/mjcf/experimental/20261104-cad_v3): x dorsal (+) / palmar (-), y along the MCP and PIP axes, z up. The yaw axis is x; v3's MCP axis lies 20.75 mm below it.

scs0009.note: len is along the case from the shaft (short end -, long end +); h is measured from the base to the spline top

lower_finger.note: the MCP link and DIP link of both designs once the PIP servo is off the finger; relative to the MCP axis (mcp_*) and the PIP axis (dip_*)

drive.note: idler on the MCP axis; a parallelogram rod to a crank on the DIP link; a parallel four-bar from the PIP servo's crank to a second arm of the idler

v4a.title: PIP servo on the yaw link
v4a.note: yaw frame coordinates; the yaw servo, yaw link and MCP servo are cad_v3's

v4b.title: Gimbal MCP with the MCP and PIP servos on the yoke
v4b.note: yoke frame coordinates, origin at the gimbal centre G on v3's yaw axis; the MCP servo stands on G, the PIP servo right behind it, the yaw servo behind both on the yaw axis; the yaw link's 20.75 mm moves into the MCP link (51.55 mm)

low_variant.note: gimbal at v3's MCP point, the 20.75 mm kept as a fixed metacarpal; replay only

v4c.title: Two-rod differential at a gimbal MCP, after the AmazingHand: two STS3032 in the carriage, the PIP servo flat on the MCP link with one rod
v4c.note: mm. Base rods in the mount frame (= the yaw frame at yaw 0), origin at G on v3's yaw axis; the PIP drive in the MCP link frame. The base geometry is the codesign's (scripts/cad/v4c_codesign.py): lugs lug_x dorsal of G and lug_y to either side at the rest pose (yaw 0, MCP mcp_rest), horns of radius horn_r on shafts along x shaft_y to either side of the finger's plane, horn_z above G. pip.side is +1 for the index (rod on its outer side, +y) and -1 for the middle.

v4c_hw.title: v4c with bought joints (2026-11-19 night): rods with a spherical bearing at the horn and an offset knuckle at the lug
v4c_hw.note: mm, the finger's mount frame with the gimbal centre G at the origin: x dorsal, y lateral, z up (toward the palm). Base pair from scripts/cad/v4c_codesign.py hardware (r 10, h 10, w 10, L 25, shafts 18.6 mm apart so the 18 mm disc horns clear); Q0 = (h, +-w, 0) is the rod's lower bearing at rest, pin 1's foot sits knuckle_e back along the rod and rod_offset_c along pin 2. PIP from the sweep of 2026-11-19: servo flat, long end toward the PIP, horn knuckle, lug bearing on a bolt along y. gimbal_below_v3_yaw_axis follows from the x-stage beam's underside (21.9 mm above v3's yaw axis) less 1 mm, the rods' height L, the horn radius and the rod end's 8 mm boss.

disc_horn.note: aluminium disc horn shipped with the STS3032 (Feetech sheet, accessories)

spherical_bearing.note: steel spherical plain bearing, RS PRO 382-380 (d 3, D 12, inner ring W 4.8, outer ring H 3.6, ball 6); tilt on a 4 mm spacer

servo_tab_holes.note: STS3032 STEP (Feetech 2020-06-09): along the case from the spline, across from its centreline
